issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a Rideable.messageOnRide() method with no parameters returning a String (and the example Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments). However, the solution implements Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (adds an int parameter) and Pig/Seal implementations include this parameter and incorporate speed in the returned string. This parameter mismatch changes the required method signature and expected output text, and would prevent students from implementing the no-argument method described in the exercise or from matching the example usage in Main.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface and all implementations use the no-argument signature specified in the problem: change Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) to messageOnRide(). Update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() and return the string in the format from the spec (e.g. "Riding on Pig Doodle"). Alternatively, if the intent is to include speed, update the problem statement, UML, and example Main to declare and call messageOnRide(int speed) consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Rideable.messageOnRide() method with no parameters that returns a string like "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". However, the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (and Pig/Seal implement messageOnRide(int speed)), changing the method signature and the returned string (it includes speed and "at X mph"). This mismatch makes the template's example calls (System.out.println(r.messageOnRide())) incompatible with the solution and will confuse students about the required method signature and return value.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem and template by changing the Rideable interface and its implementations to use messageOnRide() with no parameters and return the string exactly as specified ("Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"). Alternatively, update the problem statement and template examples to require messageOnRide(int speed) and document the expected return format (including speed) so all artifacts agree.
